I hadn’t really thought of there being any sort of stigma with keeping default handles. Some folks don’t own domains or know how to mess with dns to verify themselves. I do wonder if my default username of @cdharrison.bsky.social is now free to snag.
*good question*

@cdharrison.bsky.social
They should just hide the suffix
Something like this?

yeah—I agree with this
addendum: I’m reminded of someone linking to Bluesky on a news chyron—the .bsky.social made it clear it was a Bluesky username without an icon 👍
*exactly*
No, just hide the default bsky.social suffix
Wouldn't that lessen the verification aspects of using DNS though? Especially if they allow custom domains to hide the suffix. Seems like we'd have a spoofing issue equivalent to email.
yeah—I think the main idea is that this is a UX problem

clarifying if need be that my "green bubbles" is not pejorative:
bsky.app/profile/fvsc...
definitely a similar clique-based design problem

Like @vivainio.bsky.social said the idea is to hide “bsky.social”

Mastodon does something similar where ppl who are on the same server as you don’t have the full user handle (username + server name) displayed, just username. But those on different servers do have the full user handle displayed
So translated to Bluesky you would just leave custom domain usernames unaltered
And you don't even need a DNS record nowadays, you can "verify" your handle with a text file (provided you already have a website then)

I think it's a feature that they show the full domain for .bsky.social users. Even if it would be better for the network short term to hide it, so posts look better for everybody, my vote goes to keep it visible and use this as a nudge for them to get a domain; making it easier through bsky services
I agree with this. The alternative would preference users to *keep* their non-custom domain handles. And I say this as someone who has decided not to move over to one yet.
If this was true, it would mean bluesky intentionally makes experience worse for majority of users

This would break the “your handle is a url” convention of Bsky though.

As in vivainio.bsky.social literally links to your profile.

Yes. And I would do the same if I was taking the shots. I imagine this is intentional. They discussed and decided the pain was worth it. To be honest, I think a ton of us wouldn't set our domains if the .bsky.social would look even better. I would be @patak instead of @patak.dev
yea I'd go back to @b1mind vs @b.1mind.dev . I still come up in search either way though. I just like the consistency of it from other platforms. 🤷‍♂️

Buying domains through Bluesky already exists. It does almost all the account setup for you when you do it that way. I bought my domain that way.

Link: bsky.social/about/blog/7...
I haven't got round to it yet, okay??
This is by design and makes 100% sense. What happens if at some point we have @username.fb.social and many more . Let’s keep it
I think it would be awesome if the "you're your website" id scheme spreads everywhere. Imagine being the exact same @your.web in GitHub, Discord, and every other network
But this way I know it is you by seeing the domain and not have to rely on a weird blue checkmark
It would play into the semantic web so much more if we relied on URIs. I'd be for it.

fair enough! but now we’re here? I do think it’d be better if there were a mastodon-esque plurality of instances folks were joining—though I could see the argument that @mastodon.social is the .bsky.social in this scenario
whoa, TIL

Yes. Until we have third-party apps, a nice trick here would be that they get a few domains and rotate them when creating users. So you'll see .bsky.social, .sky.blue, .blue.app, .proto.sky, and so on. If they have ~10 of this, then I think you wouldn't have sent your post (cc @samuel.bsky.team)
petesdraincare@hotmail.com

Whats wrong with just keeping the bsky.social handle? I considered hooking it up to my website or even my github, but those are both "thepassle" because "passle" was already taken. On bsky I can just use "passle", I like that much better.
I know not of what you speak.

it doesn’t work like mastodon. bsky.social is the default domain provided by the Bluesky PDS, but if you make an account on a different PDS you’ll have a different domain. the key difference though is that you can change it at any time and it is not dependent on your PDS once you’ve made your acc

different “instances” wouldn’t appear different because there’s no such thing as other instances in mastodon terms.

however I do like the idea of getting to pick from a handful of starter domains, we have discussed this in the past
well you don't need to self host a PDS or anything for a custom handle, you need to own a domain

Apart from your handle looking better: @passle.dev vs @passle.bsky.social. The .bsky.social handle doesn't convey any social verification. There was already several variations on bun that were impersonating it. But it wasn't an issue because @bun.sh is around, so you know which one is the real one.

It verifies your identity. Of course so does linking it from your website, but it takes an extra step to check.

I have configured my domain as a handle, but I don’t like that it means someone could grab my name as a bsky.social handle
I see, and yes, you could have several bluesky managed PDS instead of a single huge one and then you get the same proposal.

it could be seen as a way to trick users into thinking that bluesky is more decentralized that what it really is regarding PDS, but I think it should be fine, and you could say that you do it because it lets you better test the network?

we do have several dozen bsky managed PDSes, each with ~500k users. They just all use “bsky.social”

what I’m trying to say is, the handle doesn’t matter. we could set it to anything. it doesn’t depend on what PDS you’re on
it’s a design goal to make decentralisation less obvious, not more obvious
ah, good to know, thanks. i haven't looked into it yet.
Ah, that's right. Sorry. Then it is just a matter of deciding to do it if you'd like. You said this was discussed before, no? What were the reasons to keep using "bsky.social" for everyone?
whats stopping someone from getting a domain similar to my name though? the-passle.dev and then pretending to be me?
I get that its different for large companies or celebrities, but for little old me, I'm not sure hooking up a domain actually verifies my identity
I guess I should stop being lazy about it

The fact that you had your domain for a long time and people trust it. For example, we know github.com, and then it doesn't matter if someone takes the-github.com. And if you move to another domain, you can redirect from your previous one and keep that trust that you built over time.

alright, well, that was incredibly easy. for anybody else looking to do the same:

bluesky > settings > account > handle > I have my own domain

can update via either .well-known file or dns

@heydonworks.bsky.social @richardiii.bsky.social

If using domains as handles would spread to other services, the story would be even better, because people will know you by that same domain everywhere, all linking to the same website. So trust you build in any of the services spreads to the others.
If I switch to a domain now, do I lose the Lists that already spent time in curating my Feeds?
Yeah thats a fair point
we're already on different mushrooms. I honestly recommend folks understand the architecture here before trying to redesign it ;)
you can change domains whenever you want, you don't lose anything
not redesigning anything here, but thanks, I would love to learn more, trying ;)
